title: This Cloud Giant Plans New Layoffs to Cover Surging AI Data Center Bill. What That Means for Investors Now.
excerpt: Oracle is planning fresh layoffs before September as debt and AI infrastructure spending squeeze cash flow, according to a new report.
content_html:
Aditya Raghunath

Thu, August 13, 2026 at 10:52 AM CDT 3 min read

Oracle (ORCL) recently posted a record quarter in fiscal Q4 of 2026 (ended in May) as revenue topped $19 billion and cloud growth accelerated. Still, the tech giant is reportedly preparing to lower its employee count, according to a Business Insider report.

Oracle Prepares New Round of Layoffs

Business Insider reported on Aug. 11:

  • Oracle has drawn up plans for a fresh round of layoffs in August, according to people familiar with the matter and an internal document.

  • Managers have reportedly been asked to submit lists of affected employees, with the goal of trimming payroll before Oracle's fiscal second quarter begins Sept. 1.

  • The cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams.

  • The company already reduced its workforce by 21,000 roles, or about 13%, during the fiscal year that ended in May, bringing headcount down to roughly 141,000 employees from 162,000 a year earlier.

  • Severance and related exit costs jumped sharply as a result, climbing to $1.84 billion for the year from just $374 million the year before.

  • Oracle has said publicly that AI adoption is one factor behind the reductions, language that rarely appears so directly in corporate filings.

Why Oracle's AI Bill Keeps Climbing

The urgency behind the cuts is not surprising given Oracle's spending pattern. The cloud infrastructure company grew sales by 17% in fiscal 2026, which is notable for a decades-old database software entity. 

However, its revenue growth is not enough to cover the cost of building out AI data centers. Oracle's capital expenditures jumped to $55.7 billion for the fiscal year ended in May 2026, up from $21.2 billion the year before and just $6.9 billion two years earlier.

The company's spending outpaced cash generation, which meant ORCL reported a free cash outflow of almost $24 billion in fiscal 2026. To cover that gap, Oracle raised $46.1 billion in long-term debt during the year and issued $5 billion in preferred stock.

Long-term debt on Oracle's balance sheet climbed to $122.3 billion as of May 2026, up from $85.3 billion the prior year. Cash from financing activities came in at $40.3 billion for the year. 

Oracle's own earnings call in June confirmed the pattern, with executives saying the company expects to raise roughly $40 billion more through a mix of debt and equity in the current fiscal year.

为什么甲骨文的人工智能账单不断攀升

考虑到甲骨文的支出模式，削减开支的紧迫性并不令人意外。 这家云基础设施公司在 2026 财年的销售额增长了 17%，这对于拥有数十年历史的数据库软件实体来说非常引人注目。

然而，其收入增长不足以覆盖建设人工智能数据中心的成本。 截至 2026 年 5 月的财年，甲骨文的资本支出跃升至 557 亿美元，高于前一年的 212 亿美元和两年前的 69 亿美元。

该公司的支出超过了现金生成，这意味着 ORCL 报告 2026 财年的自由现金流出近 240 亿美元。 为了弥补这一缺口，甲骨文在这一年筹集了 461 亿美元的长期债务，并发行了 50 亿美元的优先股。

截至 2026 年 5 月，甲骨文资产负债表上的长期债务从上一年的 853 亿美元攀升至 1,223 亿美元。 全年融资活动现金403亿美元。

甲骨文自己 6 月份的财报电话会议证实了这一模式，高管们表示，该公司预计在本财年通过债务和股权组合再筹集约 400 亿美元。
